title: The Ticket That Rang Twice
description:
Vesper’s overnight drop is already a completed-sales file — Lab 1 already threw out the junk. This morning the floor dashboard still could not total the till: web and app tickets had slipped in, some register retries padded the ticket id, and the same POS sale is on the file more than once.

This report is **in-store POS only**. Read that file from `INPUT_PATH`. Apply the rules below, then write Parquet to `OUTPUT_PATH`.

The file is the Vesper overnight sales fact (15 columns). Do not invent rows. Do not add columns. After you finish, Finance wants **one POS row per ticket**.

Use Spark DataFrame APIs. Do not `collect()` the table and loop in Python.

## Rules

These all have to be true of the file you write. They are not a recipe.

- **One row per `txn_id`.** Exact repeats and padded-id repeats are the same sale. Collapse them.
- **`txn_id`.** Strip leading and trailing spaces. The id in the output must already be trimmed.
- **`channel`.** Keep the row only when channel is exactly `POS`. `web` and `app` are out. Do not rewrite a channel token to make it match.

The other thirteen columns are already trusted. Pass them through.

## Example

Five input lines. Two POS tickets should remain.

**Input** (shown columns only)

| txn_id | channel | quantity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| t1 | POS | 2 |
| t1 | POS | 2 |
| ·t2· | POS | 1 |
| t3 | web | 4 |
| t4 | app | 3 |

(dots stand for spaces)

**Output**

| txn_id | channel | quantity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| t1 | POS | 2 |
| t2 | POS | 1 |

- t1 was written twice — one POS row remains.
- t2’s padded id is the same ticket after the spaces go.
- t3 and t4 are gone — this dashboard is POS only.

Setter notes — not shown to learners.

## What was in mind

Lab 2 of the **Vesper** overnight-sales sequence. Same 15-column fact as lab 1. This dashboard is **POS only**. The first wide op on this file is collapsing tickets.

The line we wanted them to write: two **narrow** ops, then one **wide** collapse on **`txn_id`**.

The learner brief lists those constraints **out of pipeline order** (collapse, then trim, then filter) and says they are not a recipe. Intended order is still trim → filter POS → `dropDuplicates(["txn_id"])`. Filter and trim commute; trim **must** happen before the collapse or padded twins survive.

| Step | Transform | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel` | `filter` `== "POS"` | narrow |
| `txn_id` | `trim` | narrow |
| tickets | `dropDuplicates(["txn_id"])` | wide — shuffle |

Duplicates are on **`txn_id`** (the ticket), not on store or product. This is not lab 10 (window, latest `event_ts` wins). Copies of a POS ticket are identical after trim, so any survivor is correct.

Do **not** `lower` / `replace` channel. `pos` is not `POS`. Web/app are dropped, not rewritten.

The question we wanted History to answer on a failed Submit: **did you filter POS, trim the id, then collapse on txn_id? Or skip one?**

## Why performance is light

`dropDuplicates` shuffles. AQE is off so that shuffle stays visible. Functional match still decides pass/fail. Pace is labeled from Spark History. Time never flips a pass into a fail.

## How we created the cases

Two files. 20k / 100k **unique** tickets, all starting as `POS`. Some are flipped to `web`/`app`. Extras are appended copies, so input is larger than output.

1. **`01-run-edges` (20k unique, Run)** — exact POS copies, a padded-id copy, non-POS rows.
2. **`02-submit-all` (100k unique, Submit)** — also padding on the original id, triple copies, and a duplicated non-POS ticket.

A job that only `dropDuplicates` without `trim` keeps the padded twin. A job that never filters keeps web/app. A job that `lower`s channel to keep `pos` is the wrong lesson.

Oracle is `solution/solve.py`. Official goldens are Spark-produced. Grade is a row-diff on `txn_id`.

gradeChecks: Functional: candidate Parquet matches expected on txn_id (POS only, trimmed id, one row per ticket)
